messages:
Emma (docs): Hey team — putting up a small docs PR to add a clear example of audit-log exports for SOC2 evidence. Main ask: include an export schema example + explicit redaction guidance for PII before export. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2431 :eyes:

Raj (product): thanks. Is this specifically for hosted exports, or should we cover Dedicated/Private exports too?

Emma (docs): Good q. Intend to cover all three, with a short note that Private installs may have local retention policies and legal controls. But we need one canonical JSON schema and a short redaction checklist.

Olivia (security): Can we add a concrete list of fields we consider sensitive by default? e.g., ip_address, auth_token, api_key, user_email. Also say that customers can opt-in to include hashed identifiers for correlation.

Mike (eng): I added a minimal SDK snippet to the PR showing v2 export format. If we settle on the schema I can make the ingestion example match. Current snippet:```json
POST /v2/audit/export HTTP/1.1
Host: export.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "export_id": "exp_2024_09_23_01",
  "range": {"from":"2024-09-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2024-09-23T00:00:00Z"},
  "events": [
    {
      "ts": "2024-09-01T12:34:56Z",
      "actor": {"id":"u_123","role":"user"},
      "action": "model.generate",
      "resource": "session:abc",
      "metadata": {"prompt_len":123},
      "sensitive_fields_redacted": ["user_email"]
    }
  ]
}```

Nora (devex): Could we also show a Python client example (how to download and stream the export)? Many users ask for that when migrating.

Emma (docs): Yes — I'll add the Python snippet. Also adding two short callouts: 1) "redaction-first" export: default policy redacts known PII, 2) "full-export" for enterprise with attestations + legal approval.

Alice (legal): On the "full-export" option: legal wants an audit trail that proves customer requested the full export and accepted responsibility. Add a required checkbox/consent snippet and store the consent record id in the export metadata.

Olivia (security): +1 for consent. Also add guidance on encryption-in-transit & at-rest for export bundles, and recommend SHA256 checksums for integrity verification.

Raj (product): For the docs UX, suggest small decision flow diagram: Hosted -> redacted by default; Dedicated -> configurable via admin console; Private -> controlled by local ops. Keep diagram tiny.

Mike (eng): One implementation gotcha: our previous export schema used "user_id" as an integer; new schema uses string prefixed with type (e.g., "user:u_123"). I'll include a migration note.

Emma (docs): I'll add a bolded migration note and a tiny snippet showing a transformation:```diff
- "user_id": 12345
+ "actor": {"id":"u_12345","type":"user"}
```

Nora (devex): For the SDK section, add a quick mapping table for v1 -> v2 fields and a one-liner to call out the header change (`X-Redwood-Export-Version: 2`).

Emma (docs): Draft updated in the PR. Can folks quickly sanity-check the redaction checklist and the consent metadata fields?

Olivia (security): Quick pass: checklist looks good. Suggest adding explicit phrase: "Do not rely on client-side redaction alone; server-side enforcement required."

Alice (legal): Consent metadata fields look fine: `consent_id`, `consent_ts`, `consent_requester`. Add guidance to retain the consent record per your region's retention laws.

Raj (product): LGTM from product perspective. Small wording nit: change "export bundle" to "export package" for consistency with other docs.

CI-bot: docs/pr-2431 — build passed :white_check_mark:

Emma (docs): Thanks all. I'll fold these in and request a formal review from Olivia & Alice before merging. If no objections, I'll ship tomorrow morning. :shipit:
